# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives a 3×3 lookup table: display values 4, 7, 8 against blue, green, yellow lights, producing blue/yellow/red outcomes. I will gesture a compact table to Deaf: header order blue-green-yellow, then each row identified by tally marks. I use 🖖 for blue, 👍 for green, 👌 for yellow, and 👎 for red; red/yellow/green have intuitive traffic-style associations and blue is the remaining distinct code. Deaf can then tell Blind the relevant result aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖","👍","👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","🫱","🖖","👌","👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","🫱","👎","🖖","👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","🫱","👌","👎","🖖"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel only three unlabeled wire positions. Please gesture Deaf to speak aloud every visual detail: wire colors, labels, markings, lights, and display. I can hear Deaf's speech.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🫱]

Deaf’s gesture matches the eight-count row marker, so I infer the display is 8. For display 8, the manual maps light colors in the previously sent column order—blue, green, yellow—to outputs yellow, red, blue. I repeat that row alone so Deaf can use their observed light color to select the corresponding output and tell Blind aloud.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","🫱","👌","👎","🖖"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌 👎 🖖]

Deaf’s three-symbol response repeats the display-8 output row I sent, so they appear to have received it. Blind still needs Deaf’s spoken description of the bomb; I will use an attention/pointing gesture to request that Deaf report the visible light and wire information aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵","🖐","👉","✍","🫱","🖖","👍","👌","🫱","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please ask Deaf, by gesture, to speak aloud what the display-8 gesture sequence means in terms of the visible wires: specifically which numbered wire I must cut. Do not authorize a cut until that is stated.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🫱 👌 👎 🖖]

The relevant manual entry for display 8 depends on the visible light: blue light means cut blue, green light means cut red, and yellow light means cut blue. Deaf must translate the applicable result into the numbered position of the matching visible wire and say that number aloud to Blind; no cut should occur yet. I will gesture the display-8 row again, followed by a clear “you / speak-report / point to position” style request.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","🫱","👌","👎","🖖","🫵","✍","👉","☝","✌","🤟"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: You have Deaf's spoken state: display 8, green, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Apply the manual and gesture Deaf a single unambiguous cut-wire number: one finger for wire 1, two fingers for wire 2, or three fingers for wire 3. Deaf, please speak that number aloud to me.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫵 ✍ 👉 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

With display 8 and a green light, the manual specifies red. The red wire is wire 1, so I gesture one finger to Deaf for them to say aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please now give the final manual-derived cut choice only. Gesture Deaf exactly ONE of these and no other symbol: ☝ means cut wire 1; ✌ means cut wire 2; 🤟 means cut wire 3. Deaf: speak the one received symbol's wire number aloud.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Display 8 with green light maps to red. The red wire is wire 1. I will send exactly the agreed single-symbol instruction.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```
